# Pending changes (since patch 0007, 2026-11-08)

## 2026-11-09 - Playtests: following an NPC, Skylla, the whole main quest and the home missions; dock queuing fix
- Asked: playtest following a friendly NPC for 3 minutes; Skylla again; the entire main quest and all the current
  solar system's side quests; then fix what the last one found.
- Follow (scripted, 3 min real time): steady 218-246 behind a Minoan patrol, no reversals, follow never dropped.
  (An earlier run: the followed ship was killed by a pirate at 85 s - the follow cleared and your ship coasted to
  a stop, no errors.)
- Skylla (starting ship): dead in 81 s incl. the death sequence, 118 damage, no deaths; sweep dodged 6/6; 32 s in ink.
- Main quest + missions (scripted pilot, 3x speed, starting ship never upgraded): quest taken from Kilon on Thalassa,
  all 17 stages completed in ~6 min game time (8 deaths: Asterion 2, Talos 3, near the Labyrinth 2, Minotaur 1);
  then all 30 available home-system missions (9 salvage, 6 bounty, 5 hunt, 5 supply, 3 courier, 2 survey)
  completed; credits 150 -> 63,912, Minoan reputation 26 -> 100. Goods for deliveries / salvage / supply were given
  (not mined or traded); 3 hunt targets spawned when none were around.
- Found: docking again at a station you'd just left was silently ignored while the undock animation played - no
  station menu (8 times). Fix: main.dock() queues a dock asked for during a ship animation (_dock_queued) and docks
  when it ends (_ship_anim_end).
- Tests: test_play.test_dock_during_undock_is_queued (dock, close, dock during the undock: the menu opens) - 21/21.
- Files: scripts/main.gd, tests/test_play.gd

## 2026-11-09 - Sphere shields; creatures' own bullet patterns and styles; Cerberus upgraded; waves and souls
- Asked: change the shield's shape to a sphere, always covering the entire sprite, for ships too; update Cerberus;
  (answered: how long a signal lasts); each creature its own bullet patterns, changing over time, with different
  bullet styles; Skylla's tentacle attack replaced by bullets shaped as sea waves with foam on top; Cerberus an
  extra attack of ghost bullets - souls trapped in Hades.
- Shields: a sphere whose diameter is the sprite's diagonal + 24 (ShieldEffect.sphere_for / resize) - the
  player's ship (sized from its sprite, re-sized when the ship changes), every NPC ship and every creature. The
  shader adds a sphere's light (a soft highlight up-left, a rim of light opposite). Creatures' shields drawn at 28 %.
- Cerberus: hull 2800 (was 1150) + 800 shields recovering 40/s; two attacks of his own (aimed while he winds up,
  then committed): a triple fire breath (three cones from his jaws, the side ones fanned out, 38 dps for 1.4 s)
  and a pounce (an arrow following you, then a leap at 1150 px/s to where you were, 26 damage).
- Bullet patterns (SpaceMonster: pattern_pool / _pattern_step / fight_stage / _shot; per-creature POOLS): each
  creature picks from its own pool, which changes as the fight goes on - stage 1 after 40 s or below 2/3 hull,
  stage 2 after 80 s or below 1/3 hull (denser, faster):
  - Skylla: tide (wobbling bubble waves), whirlpool (curling bubble arms), lash (ink streams in 8 directions),
    breakers (walls of foam-crested waves with a gap - replacing her tentacle sweep), ink rain, maelstrom (stage 2).
  - The Minotaur: volley (rows of spears), labyrinth (gold rings with one gap), horns (spears raking from each eye),
    stampede (spears that start slow and charge), maze (stage 2 / his phase 2).
  - Cerberus: three heads (each head's fan of fireballs), souls (pale wailing ghosts of Hades drifting after you -
    new), hellfire (scattering embers), triple spiral, firestorm, inferno (stage 2).
  The Void Leviathan keeps the old four.
- Bullet styles (Orb.STYLES): orb, bubble, ink, spear, flame, ember, wave (a breaking crescent of water, tips curling
  back, foam and spray on the crest), ghost (a pale soul with hollow eyes and a wailing mouth, a wispy tail; homes in
  at 0.55 rad/s). Orbs can wobble, accelerate and home; ink, waves and ghosts drawn normally (dark parts), the rest glow.
- Signals (answer, no change): a system's signals are regenerated every 20 minutes of play (SignalSites.EPOCH 1200 s
  of galaxy time, which pauses with the game); unlocated ones vanish at the boundary, located unfinished ones are
  kept (up to 3 per system) until done.
- Playtests (external/playtests/creature_fight.gd, starting ship): Skylla 131 s, 541 damage, no deaths; Cerberus
  82-128 s, 272-586 damage, one death at the end of one run. Style sheet: external/playtests/bullet_styles.gd.
- Tests: test_signals 9/9 (the monster fights in its own patterns), test_play 21/21, test_ships 9/9.
- Files: scripts/space_monster.gd, sea_witch.gd, minotaur_boss.gd, cerberus_beast.gd, shield_effect.gd, ship.gd,
  enemy.gd, enemy_types.gd, shaders/shield.gdshader, tests/test_signals.gd; new external/playtests/*.gd
- Fix: Cerberus' breath cones and pounce arrow were drawn with world coordinates; in a signal site (240000 out) the
  polygons lost precision ("triangulation failed", intermittently). Now drawn relative to him (and the wave bullet's
  polygon is checked before drawing). test_signals 9/9 three runs in a row.

## 2026-11-09 - Cetus and Echidna (new monster signals); creatures hunt you, follow you out of their signal
- Asked: new signal monster Cetus (top-view and side-view reference images); monsters hunt the player down when
  he goes out of range, and if he leaves the signal for the system they follow him out a few seconds later,
  attacking any NPC in their path; monster speed matched to the player's; new signal monster Echidna (top-view
  and front-view images).
- Cetus (CetusBeast; art cut by tools/cetus_parts.py: top view -> body 1552x941, fins 579x358 / 567x350, tail
  406x691; side view whole 1604x1096): unlike the others it turns with its heading. The body bends in a wave
  running head to tail (shaders/cetus_swim.gdshader, 34 art px at the tail), the tail fin and fins ride the bend
  (CetusBeast.bend, the same curve), fins beat, the tail sweeps, golden eyes glow. Hull 3000 + 800 shields.
  Patterns: tidal ring (rings of waves with a gap), spout (bubble jets from the maw), undertow (bubbles curling
  back in), whirl (two arms of waves), deluge (stage 2). Special - the dive: it sinks (0.8 s), its shadow slides
  toward you under the void (1.6 s), a ring marks where you were (1.3 s), and it BREACHES there - the side view
  leaping out (1.1 s): 32 damage inside the ring (230 px), 16 waves rolling out from its edge.
- Echidna (EchidnaBeast; tools/echidna_parts.py - background cleared by colour: the purple reaching the edge and
  large enclosed patches, soft edges; rembg left her coils half transparent): top view -> body 1214x1318, arms
  497x452 / 415x496, tail crescent 622x704; front view whole 1274x1389. Upright; arms reach and claw, tail
  sways, she breathes, eyes burn gold. Hull 2900 + 800 shields. New bullet styles: serpent (a little gold-banded
  snake slithering, tongue flicking) and venom (a glowing green drop). Patterns: fangs (two venom streams curving
  in), coil (a ring of serpents spawned round YOU, closing in - find the gap), hiss (3-arm venom spiral), nest
  (serpents every way, homing). Specials: brood (she rears up - the front view rising over her - and looses 8-12
  homing serpents) and venom (three marks following you, three globs -> acid pools of 150 px, 22 dps, 4 s).
- Hunting (Enemy._creature_target / hunting / is_creature): a creature that has once seen you never gives up the
  chase (no leash), and its speed (and at least its acceleration) matches your ship's max_speed, as upgraded;
  any NPC ship within 450 px of it is attacked first. Creature bullets now hit NPC ships too (Orb, the neutrals
  looked up once a frame).
- Following you out (new MonsterPursuit): leave a monster signal while its creature lives and hunts you, and it's
  stashed (hidden, frozen, attacks broken off: SpaceMonster.calm) - 3.5 s later "Something followed you out of the
  signal...", at 5 s it surfaces 1300 px from you, fading in, with its damage kept, hunting you. Killed there: the
  signal's loot (alien alloy, data cores, credits) and the signal done. Back into its signal: it's there, as hurt
  as it was. In another signal: it waits, and follows you out again. Jumping away loses it. Not saved.
- Library: MONSTERS room has Cetus and Echidna (room re-centred). Docs: game.md (Cetus, Echidna, hunting),
  editor.md.
- Playtests (creature_fight.gd, starting ship; also fixed there: re-chase after a dodge, dodge the breach ring):
  Cetus 85 s, 167 damage, no deaths (before the fix to the breach burst - all 16 waves spawned on you - it killed
  the ship every dive); Echidna 86 s, 271 damage, no deaths.
- Tests: test_signals 10/10 (new test_monster_follows_you_out: hunts, keeps after you beyond aggro, follows you
  out hidden, surfaces beside you as hurt as it was, not saved, attacks an NPC in its path, killed there -> done
  + alloy; test_signal_creatures covers Cetus and Echidna rigs).
- Files: scripts/cetus_beast.gd, echidna_beast.gd, monster_pursuit.gd (new), shaders/cetus_swim.gdshader (new),

## 2026-11-09 - The Hydra (new monster signal) and its double heads
- Asked: new signal monster the Hydra (top-view and front-view reference images); then a double-head sprite: each
  time the Hydra loses a portion of its health a double head appears, behaves like a normal head, follows the Hydra
  and shoots; at most 12 at once. Then: let the user playtest the Hydra (external/playtests/play_creature.gd).
- Art (tools/hydra_parts.py, cut by colour like Echidna's): top view (1536x1024) -> the knot of coils (body
  1154x969) and eight heads (about 300-480 px each) - polygons traced per head, plus every bit left outside the
  knot (eroded 13 px so thin bridges break) given to the nearest head; front view whole 1569x1090; the double head
  whole 1333x905, its two jaws and neck in the JSON.
- HydraBeast: upright; the heads weave out of step, each fires from its own jaws. Hull 3000 + 800 shields.
  Bullet styles: fang (a curved ivory tooth, its tip bloody) and miasma (a dark green poison cloud, swelling).
  Patterns: eight heads (each spits along its own neck), volley (fangs from every head at you), miasma (homing
  poison clouds), storm (all heads spinning, stage 1+). Specials: bite (the head nearest you draws back 0.55 s, a
  ring where it will strike, then darts up to 300 px on a stretched scaly neck: 24 damage + a fan of fangs) and
  breath (the front view rises; three rings of miasma with a gap).
- Double heads (HydraHead, enemy type hydra_head: 220 hull, its own ship - target it, kill it): every 1/12 of
  the Hydra's hull lost, the head nearest you is cut off (venom bursting from the stump, the head growing back in
  6 s) and a double head bursts out of the stump - max 12 alive. They keep their place round the Hydra
  (Enemy.leader / leader_slot: a slot round it, turning slowly), fire from both jaws (twin fangs, twin spit,
  twin ring; resting 3.2-4.4 s between), die with it, vanish if it dives into the void after you; not saved.
  SpaceMonster.pause: the rest between attacks, per creature.
- Bot playtest (before easing: a head every 1/16, hull 3200): 168 s, 3 deaths, 1106 damage with the starting
  ship - eased to 1/12, hull 3000, double heads resting longer.
- Tests: test_signals 10/10 (x3) - the Hydra: eight heads with their own jaws; a portion lost -> a head cut and a
  double head grown; the head grows back; more of them, at most 12; they keep round it; they die with it.
- Library: the Hydra in the MONSTERS room. Docs: game.md, editor.md.
- Files: scripts/hydra_beast.gd, hydra_head.gd (new), space_monster.gd, enemy.gd, enemy_types.gd,
  signal_site.gd, main.gd, zoo.gd, tests/test_signals.gd, docs; tools/hydra_parts.py (new);
  external/playtests/play_creature.gd (new)
- New assets: data/sprites/monster_hydra_{body,head1..head8,front,double_head}.png + monster_hydra.json;
  references in external/images/hydra/
- Fixes after the user's playtest (2026-11-09):
  - The double head drew the old procedural creature over its art (SpaceMonster._draw): HydraHead draws only its
    picture.
  - A double head's hull is 10 % of the Hydra's (HydraBeast.DOUBLE_HULL, set as it grows: 300 of 3000).
  - A double head dies quickly (0.7 s, one blast) and leaves the camera alone (SpaceMonster.cinematic /
    throes_time).
  - Camera going wild when the Hydra died (in the system): its double heads died with it, each running the
    death sequence and taking the camera at once - the later ones saved the camera's place while it was
    already off your ship and "returned" it there. Now one dying creature at a time has the camera
    (SpaceMonster._cam_taken; not taken if it's already off the ship), always given back (_give_camera_back,
    also if the creature is freed mid-throes).
  - Tests: test_signals 10/10 x2 (a tenth of the hull, a quick death, the camera back on your ship after the
    Hydra dies with its heads); test_play 21/21, test_ships 9/9, test_scenarios 4/4.

## 2026-11-09 - Playtest window position kept
- Asked: playtest windows go at the bottom-left; the game moved its window back to the centre.
- Settings._resize_window centres the window on every start; with `-- --window-at=X,Y` on the command line
  (Settings.window_at_arg) it puts it there instead. (Godot's own --position is consumed by the engine and
  overridden by that centring.) external/playtests/play_creature.gd takes it after the creature name.
- Files: scripts/settings.gd, external/playtests/play_creature.gd

## 2026-11-09 - Signal levels (easy / moderate / hard / insane); roomier cargo holds
- Asked: signal events get a level - easy, moderate, hard, insane - multiplying enemy damage and health, shown;
  then: make sure the cargo hold fits an encounter's loot easily.
- SignalSites.LEVELS: easy x0.75 (30 %), moderate x1 (35 %), hard x1.5 (23 %), insane x2.25 (12 %); level()
  is stored on new signals and drawn from the seed for old saves' (same every time). Shown: the beacon (under
  its name, "signal source · hard", and 1-4 pips in the level's colour), the scan's path labels and the
  landing tooltip ("Unknown bio-signature (Hard)"), the site's panel ("HARD x1.5", tooltip), the log.
- Its hostiles (SignalSite._spawn, empire "pirates": pirates, scavengers, ambushers, creatures - not the ship
  you're saving): hull and shields x mult; damage x mult (Enemy.damage_mult, applied in Ship.take_damage and
  Enemy.take_damage to whatever they hit - bullets, orbs, specials); hazards (the anomaly's core, the deathtrap's
  field) burn x mult; a Hydra's double heads take its damage_mult. Rewards x mult too (site drops, the pay for
  rescues; a creature that followed you out drops its signal's).
- Cargo: holds by class (Shipyard.CLASS_CARGO, prices unchanged): the starting fighter 150 (was 60), fighter 100
  (8), interceptor 80 (4), gunship 120 (12), frigate 200 (32), freighter 400 (110), explorer 160 (20), courier 140
  (16); a cargo rack +40 (16). Combat loot rolls capped at 11 per ship (Main.LOOT_ROLLS_MAX) - an insane creature
  (6750 hull) had ~97 rolls. An insane debris field (~70 units) now fills under half the smallest hold.
- Tests: full suite 112/112 (new test_signal_levels: every signal has a level, they vary, old saves get a
  stable one, the title shows it; insane: hull and shields x2.25, damage x2.25, the panel shows INSANE, rewards
  x2.25).
- Files: scripts/signal_sites.gd, signal_site.gd, signal_beacon.gd, ship_scanner.gd, landing_ui.gd, enemy.gd,
  ship.gd, hydra_beast.gd, monster_pursuit.gd, shipyard.gd, main.gd, tests/test_signals.gd
